look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check opposite simple leaves with several strong veins arching toward the tip. Feel the conspicuously rough upper leaf surface and inspect hairs beneath; when fruiting, look for clusters of white drupes carried on reddish stalks. The staged fruit photograph shows white fruit and reddish pedicels, not the diagnostic leaf hairs.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Cornus drummondii C.A.Mey. at species rank. Approved source-pool concept is species-level; do not confuse with other opposite-leaved dogwoods or infer county-native certification from a statewide occurrence.

project_inclusion.notes: Keep county-native determination UNRESOLVED internally; no three-target-county PASS asserted. No native/range badge on ordinary learner card.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous, often colony-forming multi-stemmed shrub or small tree; suckering growth can create thickets.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Leaves opposite, simple and usually ovate to elliptic with mostly entire margins; upper surface notably rough to touch, underside pubescent; several prominent lateral veins curve toward the tip.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Numerous small, four-parted whitish flowers in broad, flat-topped terminal clusters; confirm flower structure with a close-up.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Clusters of rounded whitish drupes, often on pink-red to reddish pedicels; photograph documents this character, not a leaf close-up.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Opposite leaf scars and branch arrangement; inspect young twig hairs and bark when leaves are absent.

confused_with: Cornus sericea (red-osier dogwood; usually smoother leaf surface and striking red stems, especially in winter; check fruit, veins and twig characters)
Cornus racemosa (gray dogwood; white fruits on conspicuous reddish pedicels also possible, so check rough upper leaf texture and pubescence rather than fruit color alone)
Viburnum spp. (opposite leaves in many species, but vein patterns, flowers and fruit type differ)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the combination of opposite leaves, strongly arcuate venation, rough upper leaf texture and white drupes on reddish pedicels. White fruits alone are not diagnostic.
